problem: Learned visual PointNav policies assume idealized cylinder agents and ignore the dynamics of legged robots (turning radius, speed, slipping, falling). A policy trained on one legged robot also degrades on other legged robots, so learning per robot is expensive, especially on hardware.
motivation: Legged robots are well suited to indoor homes, but visual navigation policies do not account for their dynamics. Zero-shot cross-robot transfer drops sharply (e.g. AlienGo success falls from 0.40 to 0.26 when using a Daisy-trained policy), and an A* oracle for a point agent also degrades on legged robots. A shared policy with a small learned robot-specific latent could pool data across robots and adapt quickly to new robots.
key_idea: Train a hierarchical PointNav policy (SAC+AE, depth-only) shared across several legged robots, conditioned on a learned 1-D robot-specific embedding produced by a per-robot z-network; adapt to new robots by grid-searching only that embedding while the policy stays fixed.
insight: A fully learned embedding generalizes better than fixed or dynamics-parameter-informed embeddings, especially out of distribution. On 4-legged Daisy, Learned-z gets SPL 0.49, versus 0.38 for Fixed-z, 0.22 for No-z and 0.40 for Informed-z. Informed-z is also sensitive to which parameters are chosen: Semi-Informed-z is poor on cart-pole. Ignoring dynamics hurts, as the A* oracle drops to 0.18 SPL on Daisy4 although it reaches 0.92 SPL on an idealized cylinder agent.
method: Hierarchical control: the high-level policy outputs 2-D CoM velocities (v_des, ω_des) at 4 Hz, and a shared low-level footstep planner (Raibert-style feedback) plus robot-specific IK tracks them. On hardware the stance legs use whole-body MPC.

Universal navigation policy: a SAC actor and critic shared across robots, taking an egocentric depth image, the polar goal vector and the embedding z. Depth is encoded by a 4-layer conv autoencoder to a 50-D latent (SAC+AE), and the MLPs have 3 layers of 1024 units.

Robot-specific embedding: for each robot i, a 3-layer, 100-unit MLP z-network with a learned scalar input outputs a 1-D z_i. It is trained through the critic loss using only robot i's replay buffer, while the critic's shared parameters use pooled data from all robots.

Multi-robot parallel training: robots collect experience in separate iGibson environments via multiprocessing into a shared replay buffer. The actor is updated on pooled data without updating the embeddings, giving N times more data.
Adaptation to new robots: keep the policy fixed and grid-search z in [-1,1] to maximize episode return on the new robot. On hardware, the z learned in simulation is reused with no optimization.
Reward: geodesic-distance progress, -1 for collision, -5 for a fall (which ends the episode), and +10 for success. Success means within 0.36 m of the goal in under 150 steps.

setting.backbone: SAC+AE (conv autoencoder depth encoder + MLP actor/critic) with learned robot embeddings, trained from scratch; the low-level controller is expert-designed
setting.training_data: RL in iGibson (Pybullet) home scans, 3 robots (A1, AlienGo, Daisy), 1M cumulative simulation steps across robots; no extra data
setting.observation: egocentric depth image + egomotion/localization + relative goal (polar)
setting.action_space: continuous CoM linear and angular velocity commands (v, ω), converted to footsteps by a low-level controller
setting.simulator: iGibson (Pybullet); MuJoCo for the cart-pole experiments
setting.privileged: none for the learned policy (the A* oracle baseline uses a map)

numbers.extra: z grid-searched on the new robot; policy trained on A1, AlienGo and Daisy; 5 seeds
z grid-searched on the new robot; 5 seeds

numbers_note: Not a standard VLN or ObjectNav benchmark. The real A1 hardware results are qualitative only (Fig. 10), with no numbers. The cart-pole results are in Table II (e.g. Learned-z CP4 0.94 episode reward).
results: Learned-z reaches SPL 0.48 on Laikago and 0.49 on 4-legged Daisy, beating Informed-z (0.37 and 0.40), Fixed-z (0.47 and 0.38), No-z (0.33 and 0.22), Meta-RL (<0.15) and the A* oracle (0.38 and 0.18). The policy also transfers zero-shot to a real A1 robot in a new home with the sim-learned z, though it turns close to obstacles.
limitations: The real-robot evidence is qualitative only. Hardware dynamics differ (slower turning), causing collisions, and z was not optimized on hardware.
The low-level controller is shared and imperfect, so robots fall at high velocities. Grid search over z only works for a low-dimensional embedding (1-D here).
The evaluation covers only 5 robots in simulation, with SPL of ~0.5 (absolute performance is modest).
